claim: 'Contributed to United's relegation' repeats a well-known myth. Denis Law's 1974 backheel for City did not send United down — results elsewhere that afternoon meant United were relegated regardless of the outcome of that match. The keyed scorer is correct; the causal claim in the stem is the standard false version of the story.
q: In 1974 a famous backheeled goal by a former Manchester United star, then playing for City, contributed to United's relegation. Who scored it?

claim: The stem already says it is 'a record for the fastest-ever goal' and then offers 10s / 30s / 45s / 90s. A reader with zero football knowledge picks the most extreme option by superlative logic alone, without knowing anything about Makaay or the Champions League.
q: In 2007 Bayern's Roy Makaay set a record for the fastest-ever goal in a Champions League match. Roughly how quick was it?

claim: The stem names the duo 'LuLa' and names Lukaku as one half, so the other half must begin 'La' — Lautaro Martinez is the only option starting with those letters (Icardi, Dybala, Correa do not). Decodable from the stem without football knowledge.
q: Which Argentine striker has captained Inter and formed the prolific 'LuLa' strike duo with Romelu Lukaku?

q: AC Milan share their San Siro home stadium with which city rival?

claim: Stem asserts Edwin van der Sar "returned to the club in 2016". He actually rejoined Ajax in 2012 as marketing director; 2016 is when he was promoted to general director (CEO). The keyed answer (General director/CEO) is right, but the stated return year is wrong by four years and a player learns a false fact.
q: Edwin van der Sar, Ajax's legendary goalkeeper, returned to the club in 2016 in which off-pitch capacity?

claim: Stem says Drogba "played for Galatasaray between 2013 and 2015". He signed in January 2013 and left in July 2014 to rejoin Chelsea — he never played a 2014-15 match for Galatasaray. The window should be 2013-2014.
q: Which Ivorian striker and Chelsea great played for Galatasaray between 2013 and 2014?
